clue.text: Fat and short politician

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the word before loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A description of a stocky, rotund politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short politician' looks like one unit, but 'short' trims the 'and' (PLUS), and the politician stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump is a mild adjective for someone carrying extra weight, a gentler synonym.

clue.text: Trump perhaps remaining under pressure

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written under another simply follows it

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
someone remaining in a place lives there

explanation.surface: A political jibe about Trump hanging on in office under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump has held the office of US President, so he is an example of one, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Upper-class twit and European get together

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A posh fool and a continental meet up.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join or come together, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Secret, Tommy?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a Tommy is a British soldier, typically of the lowest rank

explanation.walkthrough: Tommy, or Tommy Atkins, is the old nickname for an ordinary British soldier; the question mark flags that he is one example of the rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means confidential as an adjective and names the lowest army rank as a noun.

clue.text: Controversial issue animated King Edward, possibly

parts.note: King Edward is a well-known British potato variety

explanation.surface: An excited King Edward suggests a royal stirring up controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is not a monarch here but a variety of potato common in British shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a matter too sensitive or awkward to handle.

clue.text: Difficult keeping ordinary small squirrels away

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: It is hard work for a small creature to keep stashing its winter stores.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirrel away is an idiom for stockpiling, which is what someone who hoards does.

clue.text: Tense about a certain value

explanation.surface: Someone is nervous about a definite valuation.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure is a verb meaning to prize or hold dear, as is value.

clue.text: Arrive after incorrect result

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the second

parts.note: out as in wide of the mark, wrong

explanation.surface: Arriving late yields the wrong result.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or end result of something.

clue.text: Acknowledgement from District Attorney turning up with assignment

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: a task one is sent on

explanation.surface: A prosecutor shows up on a job and makes a confession.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is an acknowledgement or confession that something is true.

clue.text: Move falteringly taking top off stranger

indicators.note: removing the top of a down word means dropping its first letter

explanation.surface: A doddering person removes their hat in front of an unfamiliar visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' reads as a noun, a person; it is the comparative adjective meaning more peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Odder is the comparative of odd, meaning more strange or unusual.

clue.text: Get rid of priest friend hides at home

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest, a crossword regular

indicators.note: a thing that hides another keeps it tucked inside

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: An instruction to dispose of a cleric whose friend hides out at his house.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate is to remove or dispose of something completely.

clue.text: Some lad imitated retreating chicken

indicators.note: something retreating goes backwards, so the letters run right to left
some means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: a run of consecutive letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A boy did an impression of a chicken running away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' sits at the end as an animal for the impression, but it is the slang for cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone chicken is slang for cowardly, so it means fearful or timid.

clue.text: Country clubs in denial, unfortunately

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the letters that follow
something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: A nation's sports clubs are sadly in denial.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is a North Atlantic island nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: Apron's so tangled adult's scratched back

indicators.note: tangled things are twisted out of their order
something scratched from a list is struck out and removed

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A twisted apron strap has left an adult with a scratch on the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like the body part that got scratched; it is the verb meaning to support financially.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponsor someone is to back them with money or support.

clue.text: Simpler answer in test, essentially, that is right

indicators.note: in puts the preceding piece inside the following one
the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are kept

explanation.surface: A student hopes an answer in a test will be the easy, correct one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' together gives IE, the abbreviation of Latin id est.
explanation.definitionFit: Easier is the comparative of easy, meaning less difficult.

clue.text: Frightening bird grabbing rodent's tail

indicators.note: grabbing something means holding it, so one piece goes inside
a tail is the end, so only the last letter is kept

explanation.surface: A scary picture of a bird snatching a rat by the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means alarming or causing sudden fright.

clue.text: Welcome sound of a bell after endless hunger

indicators.note: without an end, so the word's last letter is dropped
after places the bell sound behind the other piece

parts.note: the ringing note of a small bell

explanation.surface: A dinner bell greets the starving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of' suggests a homophone, but TING is simply the noise a bell makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting is a welcome given on meeting someone.

clue.text: Reportedly irritate nude group of stars

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: to grate is to irritate; bare means nude

explanation.surface: Someone claims a nude person is annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Bear, Ursa Major, is a constellation, a named group of stars.

clue.text: Get rude apes bananas

indicators.note: going bananas is slang for going crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An instruction to fetch bananas for some ill-mannered apes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the apes' food, but it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To get someone to do something is to persuade or induce them.

clue.text: Each Conservative inside steals buns

indicators.note: inside places the preceding pieces within the following word

explanation.surface: Every Tory in the building pinches the buns.
explanation.walkthrough: Teacakes are a British baked treat: light, sweet, often fruited buns usually served toasted and buttered.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a type of sweet bun, so plural buns matches plural teacakes.

clue.text: Leave a party with old knight

parts.note: a party as in a group of people
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of a party alongside an elderly knight.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to desert or leave behind.

clue.text: Worth embracing new pop star?

indicators.note: embracing means wrapping around, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fresh pop star is worth the hype.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Prince was the American pop star.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince, the Minneapolis singer behind Purple Rain, was a famous pop musician.

clue.text: Puts back wheels again?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: replaces something where it was
second meaning: read as ..., turns once more, as a wheel does

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split of the word into RE plus TURNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns means puts back, and broken up it means turns again, like wheeling round once more.

clue.text: Male insect is creature with large, spiny forelegs

explanation.surface: A field-guide description of a male insect with big spiked front legs.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence of natural history, but the first three words are the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The mantis is an insect known for its raised, spiked front legs used to seize prey.

clue.text: Stay away from young lady's weapon

parts.note: to cut a class is to skip it

explanation.surface: A warning to keep clear of a girl's weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword, the classic pirate weapon.

clue.text: Hiding place a child found in church

indicators.note: something found in a place is located inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A child is discovered hiding out in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a secret store or hiding place for valuables or supplies.

clue.text: Pull half of that belt

indicators.note: half of a word means keeping only two of its four letters

parts.note: a belt of land is a tract

explanation.surface: An instruction to tug on part of a belt.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to pull or draw towards, as a magnet does.

clue.text: A struggle before mobile finally is switched on

indicators.note: before places the struggle ahead of the next piece
finally points to the very end, so only the last letter is used

explanation.surface: A battle to get a mobile phone turned on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switched on' reads as a phone being turned on; it is slang for alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Switched on is informal for alert or well informed, which is what aware means.

clue.text: Shouted about wine crossing Italy

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so the wine word spans the country letter

parts.note: I is Italy's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: Someone yelled about wine on a trip across Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry out is to shout, so cried is a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: What patient might get a newspaper career, unusually?

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Wondering what career a patient might be offered by a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftercare is the follow-up treatment a patient receives after hospital or surgery.

clue.text: Plots in Greene's novel

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: Plot points in one of Graham Greene's novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plots' looks like a noun, story lines of a novel; it is the verb meaning contrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer an outcome is to contrive or plot it, so engineers means plots.

clue.text: Curse from don after start of seminar

indicators.note: after places the don word behind the other piece
the start is the beginning, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: A university lecturer swears as a seminar gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like the university lecturer; it is the verb meaning put on.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to curse, using bad language.
